These datasets are curated for ECO 230. Each release is immutable: the files at a versioned URL will not be silently replaced. Download only the tables your question requires, preserve their row grain, and validate every join.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start here

Each dataset page explains the available files, what one row represents, the useful join keys, common analytical mistakes, and a short R example. Parquet files are smaller and faster than equivalent CSV files and preserve dates and numeric types.
:::

## Reading Parquet in R

Install `arrow` once if it is not already in the project, then read a file directly from the course data service.

```r
install.packages("arrow")

library(arrow)

data <- read_parquet("https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/olist/olist_order_analysis.parquet")
```

For reproducible work, keep the versioned URL in your script. Do not replace it with an unversioned "latest" link.

## General joining rule

Before joining two files, answer three questions:

1. What does one row represent in each file?
2. Is the join one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many?
3. What should one row represent after the join?

If either side has multiple rows per join key, aggregate it to the intended analysis grain before joining. A larger row count after a join is sometimes correct, but it must be understood and documented.
